references.title: The preconception Mediterranean dietary pattern in couples undergoing in vitro fertilization/intracytoplasmic sperm injection treatment increases the chance of pregnancy
references.finding: High couple adherence to a Mediterranean dietary pattern was associated with higher pregnancy odds after IVF/ICSI (OR 1.4) and higher folate and vitamin B6 in blood and follicular fluid.

references.authors: Muffone ARMC, de Oliveira Lübke PDP, Rabito EI
references.title: Mediterranean diet and infertility: a systematic review with meta-analysis of cohort studies
references.finding: Pooled evidence linking Mediterranean diet adherence to live birth and pregnancy was inconsistent and insufficient to support clinical application.

references.authors: Gaskins AJ, Chavarro JE
references.title: Diet and fertility: a review
references.finding: Review: supplemental folic acid (above neural-tube-defect doses) is consistently associated with better fertility; antioxidant supplements do not help women in fertility treatment; omega-3s appear beneficial; vitamin D matters mainly in deficiency.

references.authors: Chavarro JE, Rich-Edwards JW, Rosner BA, et al.
references.title: Diet and lifestyle in the prevention of ovulatory disorder infertility
references.finding: Highest vs lowest quintile of a 'fertility diet' score was associated with 66% lower risk of ovulatory infertility (RR 0.34); five or more low-risk lifestyle factors with 69% lower risk.

references.authors: Gaskins AJ, Afeiche MC, Wright DL, et al.
references.title: Dietary folate and reproductive success among women undergoing assisted reproduction
references.finding: Supplemental folate >800 ug/day vs <400 ug/day was associated with a 20 percentage-point higher live birth rate after ART.

references.authors: Cueto HT, Riis AH, Hatch EE, et al.
references.title: Folic acid supplementation and fecundability: a Danish prospective cohort study
references.finding: Folic acid or multivitamin supplementation was associated with higher fecundability (FR 1.15), more so with irregular cycles.

references.authors: US Preventive Services Task Force
references.title: Folic Acid Supplementation to Prevent Neural Tube Defects: US Preventive Services Task Force Reaffirmation Recommendation Statement
references.finding: USPSTF: everyone planning or capable of pregnancy should take a daily supplement containing 0.4-0.8 mg (400-800 ug) folic acid (A recommendation).

references.authors: Chu J, Gallos I, Tobias A, et al.
references.title: Vitamin D and assisted reproductive treatment outcome: a systematic review and meta-analysis
references.finding: Vitamin D-replete women undergoing ART had higher live birth than deficient/insufficient women (OR 1.33); no association with miscarriage.

references.authors: Zhou X, Wu X, Luo X, et al.
references.title: Effect of Vitamin D Supplementation on In Vitro Fertilization Outcomes: A Trial Sequential Meta-Analysis of 5 Randomized Controlled Trials
references.finding: In vitamin D-deficient infertile women, supplementation raised chemical pregnancy (RR 1.53) but not clinical pregnancy (RR 1.34, NS) or embryo quality.

references.authors: Chiu YH, Karmon AE, Gaskins AJ, et al.
references.title: Serum omega-3 fatty acids and treatment outcomes among women undergoing assisted reproduction
references.finding: Each 1% higher serum long-chain omega-3 was associated with 8% higher probability of live birth after ART.

references.authors: Nehra D, Le HD, Fallon EM, et al.
references.title: Prolonging the female reproductive lifespan and improving egg quality with dietary omega-3 fatty acids
references.finding: In mice, omega-3-rich diets prolonged reproductive function and improved oocyte quality at advanced maternal age; omega-6-rich diets worsened it.

references.authors: Showell MG, Mackenzie-Proctor R, Jordan V, et al.
references.title: Antioxidants for female subfertility
references.finding: Very low-quality evidence: antioxidants might raise live birth (OR 1.81) but evidence is unreliable; 2026 editorial note: 7 included trials since retracted and 2 under expression of concern (conclusions retained).

references.authors: Xu Y, Nisenblat V, Lu C, et al.
references.title: Pretreatment with coenzyme Q10 improves ovarian response and embryo quality in low-prognosis young women with decreased ovarian reserve: a randomized controlled trial
references.n: 186 women <35 with poor ovarian reserve (169 analysed)
references.finding: CoQ10 600 mg/day (200 mg three times daily) for 60 days before IVF increased oocytes retrieved (median 4 vs 2), fertilization and good embryos; live birth 29% vs 16% was not statistically significant.

references.authors: Ben-Meir A, Burstein E, Borrego-Alvarez A, et al.
references.title: Coenzyme Q10 restores oocyte mitochondrial function and fertility during reproductive aging
references.finding: Oocyte ageing in mice and humans involves reduced CoQ-synthesis enzymes and lower ATP; CoQ10 reversed age-related oocyte deficits in mice.

references.authors: Florou P, Anagnostis P, Theocharis P, et al.
references.title: Does coenzyme Q(10) supplementation improve fertility outcomes in women undergoing assisted reproductive technology procedures? A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized-controlled trials
references.finding: CoQ10 increased clinical pregnancy (28.8% vs 14.1%; OR 2.44) but not live birth (OR 1.67, NS) or miscarriage.

references.authors: Zhang Y, Zhang C, Shu J, et al.
references.title: Adjuvant treatment strategies in ovarian stimulation for poor responders undergoing IVF: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
references.finding: In poor responders, DHEA (OR 2.46) and CoQ10 (OR 2.22) were associated with higher clinical pregnancy vs control; CoQ10 had the lowest cancellation rate.

references.authors: Hu KL, Ye X, Wang S, et al.
references.title: Melatonin Application in Assisted Reproductive Technology: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials
references.finding: Melatonin increased clinical pregnancy (OR 1.43) and oocyte/embryo counts but not live birth (OR 1.38, 3 RCTs, NS); low-quality evidence.

references.authors: Fernando S, Wallace EM, Rombauts L, et al.
references.title: The effect of melatonin on ultrasound markers of follicular development: A double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial
references.journal: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
references.finding: Melatonin 2, 4 or 8 mg twice daily during IVF stimulation did not change follicle number or ovarian vascular indices vs placebo (pilot).

references.authors: Showell MG, Mackenzie-Proctor R, Jordan V, et al.
references.title: Inositol for subfertile women with polycystic ovary syndrome
references.finding: Very low-quality evidence; uncertain whether myo-inositol improves live birth (OR 2.42, 95% CI 0.75-7.83) or clinical pregnancy in PCOS before IVF.

references.authors: Fitz V, Graca S, Mahalingaiah S, et al.
references.title: Inositol for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis to Inform the 2023 Update of the International Evidence-based PCOS Guidelines
references.finding: For the 2023 PCOS guideline: inositol evidence is limited and inconclusive; possible metabolic benefits; little difference from metformin for reproductive outcomes.

references.authors: Pacchiarotti A, Carlomagno G, Antonini G, et al.
references.title: Effect of myo-inositol and melatonin versus myo-inositol, in a randomized controlled trial, for improving in vitro fertilization of patients with polycystic ovarian syndrome
references.finding: RETRACTED (2026). Claimed myo-inositol 4 g + folic acid 400 ug + melatonin 3 mg improved oocyte and embryo quality; should not be relied on.

references.authors: Thakker D, Raval A, Patel I, et al.
references.title: N-acetylcysteine for polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled clinical trials
references.finding: NAC improved ovulation and pregnancy vs placebo but was inferior to metformin; trials had high risk of bias.

references.authors: Rizk AY, Bedaiwy MA, Al-Inany HG
references.title: N-acetyl-cysteine is a novel adjuvant to clomiphene citrate in clomiphene citrate-resistant patients with polycystic ovary syndrome
references.finding: NAC 1.2 g/day added to clomiphene raised ovulation (49.3% vs 1.3%) and pregnancy (21.3% vs 0%) vs placebo.

references.authors: Naik S, Lepine S, Nagels HE, et al.
references.title: Androgens (dehydroepiandrosterone or testosterone) for women undergoing assisted reproduction
references.finding: Cochrane: DHEA probably makes little or no difference to live birth in poor responders (OR 1.30, NS, moderate certainty); testosterone probably improves it (OR 2.53).

references.authors: Wiser A, Gonen O, Ghetler Y, et al.
references.title: Addition of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) for poor-responder patients before and during IVF treatment improves the pregnancy rate: a randomized prospective study
references.finding: DHEA 75 mg/day before and during IVF was associated with higher live birth (23.1% vs 4.0%) in a very small trial.

references.authors: Ismail AM, Hamed AH, Saso S, et al.
references.title: Adding L-carnitine to clomiphene resistant PCOS women improves the quality of ovulation and the pregnancy rate. A randomized clinical trial
references.journal: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
references.finding: RETRACTED. Claimed L-carnitine 3 g/day with clomiphene raised pregnancy from 5.8% to 51.5%; should not be relied on.

references.authors: Ochiai A, Kuroda K
references.title: Preconception resveratrol intake against infertility: Friend or foe?
references.finding: Resveratrol may support ovarian function via SIRT1 but suppresses endometrial decidualization (anti-deciduogenic) and its teratogenicity is unknown; avoid in the luteal phase and pregnancy.

references.authors: Ochiai A, Kuroda K, Ikemoto Y, et al.
references.title: Influence of resveratrol supplementation on IVF-embryo transfer cycle outcomes
references.finding: Resveratrol 200 mg/day during embryo-transfer cycles was associated with lower clinical pregnancy (OR 0.54) and higher miscarriage (OR 2.60).

references.authors: Ardehjani NA, Agha-Hosseini M, Nashtaei MS, et al.
references.title: Resveratrol ameliorates mitochondrial biogenesis and reproductive outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome undergoing assisted reproduction: a randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial
references.finding: Resveratrol 800 mg/day for 60 days lowered follicular fluid oxidative stress and raised oocyte maturity and good-quality embryos, but pregnancy rates did not differ.

references.authors: Di Tucci C, Galati G, Mattei G, et al.
references.title: The role of alpha lipoic acid in female and male infertility: a systematic review
references.finding: Systematic review (28 articles): alpha-lipoic acid shows some positive effects on oocyte maturation, embryo grade and endometriosis pain, but clinical evidence is limited and more trials are needed.

references.authors: ESHRE Add-ons working group; Lundin K, Bentzen JG, et al.
references.title: Good practice recommendations on add-ons in reproductive medicine†
references.finding: ESHRE add-ons recommendations: antioxidant therapy lacks reliable evidence of higher live birth and is not recommended in ART; routine adjuncts (GH, DHEA, testosterone, metformin) are not supported.

references.authors: ESHRE Guideline Group on Ovarian Stimulation; Bosch E, Broer S, et al.
references.title: ESHRE guideline: ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI(†)
references.finding: ESHRE ovarian stimulation guideline: hormone pre-treatment and adjuvants (metformin, growth hormone, testosterone, DHEA, aspirin, sildenafil) are not recommended for improving efficacy.

references.authors: Dechanet C, Anahory T, Mathieu Daude JC, et al.
references.title: Effects of cigarette smoking on reproduction
references.finding: Systematic review: cigarette smoke contains thousands of toxicants (nicotine, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, cadmium) that target folliculogenesis, steroidogenesis and every other reproductive stage, dose-dependently.

references.authors: Hahn KA, Wise LA, Rothman KJ, et al.
references.title: Caffeine and caffeinated beverage consumption and risk of spontaneous abortion
references.finding: Preconception caffeine was not associated with miscarriage (HR 1.09 for >=300 vs <100 mg/day), whereas early-pregnancy intake of 100-299 mg/day was (HR ~1.5-1.6).

references.authors: Lim SS, Hutchison SK, Van Ryswyk E, et al.
references.title: Lifestyle changes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome
references.finding: Cochrane: lifestyle interventions in PCOS may modestly reduce weight and free androgen index; no trial reported live birth or miscarriage.

references.authors: Szymanska KJ, Tan X, Oktay K
references.title: Unraveling the mechanisms of chemotherapy-induced damage to human primordial follicle reserve: road to developing therapeutics for fertility preservation and reversing ovarian aging
references.finding: Gonadotoxic chemotherapy (e.g. cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin) induces DNA double-strand breaks and apoptosis of primordial-follicle oocytes within 12-24 h, plus stromal and microvascular damage.

references.authors: Fernando S, Biggs SN, Horne RSC, et al.
references.title: The impact of melatonin on the sleep patterns of women undergoing IVF: a double blind RCT
references.finding: Melatonin 2, 4 or 8 mg twice daily from cycle day 2 to egg retrieval did not cause daytime sleepiness or change objective sleep vs placebo.

references.authors: Abdelazeem B, Abbas KS, Shehata J, et al.
references.title: The effects of curcumin as dietary supplement for patients with polycystic ovary syndrome: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
references.finding: Curcumin improved fasting glucose (-3.7 mg/dL), insulin, HOMA-IR (-0.55) and total cholesterol, with no effect on LDL, HDL, sex hormones, weight or CRP.

references.authors: Azami SH, Nazarian H, Abdollahifar MA, et al.
references.title: The antioxidant curcumin postpones ovarian aging in young and middle-aged mice.
references.finding: In mice, intraperitoneal curcumin (100 mg/kg/day) preserved follicle numbers, AMH and oocyte quality with age.

references.authors: Chen CC, Chan WH
references.title: Injurious effects of curcumin on maturation of mouse oocytes, fertilization and fetal development via apoptosis.
references.finding: In mice, curcumin (in vitro and 40 uM in drinking water) impaired oocyte maturation, fertilisation and early embryo development via apoptosis.

references.authors: Chien YJ, Chang CY, Wu MY, et al.
references.title: Effects of Curcumin on Glycemic Control and Lipid Profile in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis and Trial Sequential Analysis.
references.finding: Curcumin improved fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR (-0.32), HDL and total cholesterol but not LDL or triglycerides.

references.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Additives and Nutrient Sources added to Food (ANS)
references.title: Scientific Opinion on the re-evaluation of curcumin (E 100) as a food additive.
references.finding: Set an ADI of 3 mg/kg bw/day for curcumin, from a NOAEL of 250-320 mg/kg bw/day (lower F2 body-weight gain in a reproductive toxicity study) with a 100-fold uncertainty factor; not carcinogenic or genotoxic.

references.authors: Feghhi F, Ghaznavi H, Sheervalilou R, et al.
references.title: Effects of metformin and curcumin in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: A factorial clinical trial.
references.finding: Nanocurcumin 80 mg three times daily plus metformin improved lipids, glucose markers, weight and testosterone more than either agent alone or placebo over 12 weeks.

references.authors: Ghanbarzadeh-Ghashti N, Ghanbari-Homaie S, Shaseb E, et al.
references.title: The effect of Curcumin on metabolic parameters and androgen level in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a randomized controlled trial.
references.finding: 1000 mg/day curcumin for 12 weeks lowered fasting glucose and reduced amenorrhoea/oligomenorrhoea (13% vs 22%) versus placebo, but did not change lipids, insulin, SHBG, testosterone or hirsutism.

references.authors: Gudarzi R, Shabani F, Mohammad-Alizadeh-Charandabi S, et al.
references.title: Effect of curcumin on painful symptoms of endometriosis: A triple-blind randomized controlled trial.
references.finding: Curcumin 1000 mg/day for 8 weeks did not improve endometriosis pain or quality of life versus placebo.

references.authors: Jannatifar R, Asa E, Cheraghi E, et al.
references.title: Nanomicelle curcumin improves oxidative stress, inflammatory markers, and assisted reproductive techniques outcomes in endometriosis cases: a randomized clinical trial.
references.n: 50 women with stage III/IV endometriosis undergoing ART
references.finding: Nanomicelle curcumin 120 mg/day for 10 weeks improved serum and follicular-fluid oxidative-stress markers and reported more oocytes, mature oocytes and good embryos; small single-centre trial.

references.authors: Mohammadi S, Ziaei S, Morvaridi M, et al.
references.title: Impacts of Curcumin Supplementation on Cardiometabolic Risk Factors in Patients With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: Curcumin modestly lowered fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR (SMD -0.36) and TC, but did not change BMI, testosterone, DHEA, LH or FSH.

references.authors: Simental-Mendía LE, Shah N, Sathyapalan T, et al.
references.title: Effect of Curcumin on Glycaemic and Lipid Parameters in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
references.finding: Curcumin lowered fasting glucose (-3.7 mg/dL), insulin and HOMA-IR (-0.94, I2 90%) but did not change any lipid index.

references.authors: Axelsson AS, Tubbs E, Mecham B, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane reduces hepatic glucose production and improves glucose control in patients with type 2 diabetes.
references.finding: Broccoli sprout extract (150 µmol sulforaphane/day, 12 weeks) reduced fasting blood glucose and HbA1c in obese patients with dysregulated type 2 diabetes (not in the whole group); in cells and animals sulforaphane suppressed hepatic gluconeogenesis via NRF2.

references.authors: Esfandyari S, Aleyasin A, Noroozi Z, et al.
references.title: The Protective Effect of Sulforaphane against Oxidative Stress through Activation of NRF2/ARE Pathway in Human Granulosa Cells.
references.finding: Sulforaphane pretreatment protected human granulosa cells from H2O2-induced ROS and apoptosis via NRF2, SOD and catalase.

references.authors: Feng Z, Wang T, Sun Y, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane suppresses paraquat-induced oxidative damage in bovine in vitro-matured oocytes through Nrf2 transduction pathway.
references.finding: 1 µM sulforaphane during in vitro maturation raised bovine oocyte maturation and embryo rates and countered paraquat oxidative damage via Nrf2.

references.authors: Li WJ, Zhang X, Shen M, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane alleviates the meiosis defects induced by 3-nitropropionic acid in mouse oocytes.
references.finding: Sulforaphane alleviated 3-nitropropionic-acid-induced meiotic, spindle and mitochondrial defects in mouse oocytes matured in vitro.

references.authors: Sohel MMH, Konca Y, Akyuz B, et al.
references.title: Concentration dependent antioxidative and apoptotic effects of sulforaphane on bovine granulosa cells in vitro.
references.finding: In bovine granulosa cells, low sulforaphane (2 µM) activated NRF2 antioxidant genes while concentrations above ~15 µM were cytotoxic.

references.authors: Taheri M, Hayati Roudbari N, Amidi F, et al.
references.title: The protective effect of sulforaphane against oxidative stress in granulosa cells of patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) through activation of AMPK/AKT/NRF2 signaling pathway.
references.n: granulosa cells from PCOS and control women (in vitro)
references.finding: Sulforaphane reduced ROS and apoptosis in granulosa-lutein cells from women with PCOS, with AMPK/AKT/NRF2 activation.

references.authors: Gharaei R, Alyasin A, Mahdavinezhad F, et al.
references.title: Randomized controlled trial of astaxanthin impacts on antioxidant status and assisted reproductive technology outcomes in women with polycystic ovarian syndrome.
references.finding: 8 mg/day astaxanthin for 40 days raised serum antioxidant capacity, granulosa-cell Nrf2 targets, and MII-oocyte and top-quality embryo rates, but not pregnancy rates.

references.authors: Rostami S, Alyasin A, Saedi M, et al.
references.title: Astaxanthin ameliorates inflammation, oxidative stress, and reproductive outcomes in endometriosis patients undergoing assisted reproduction: A randomized, triple-blind placebo-controlled clinical trial.
references.finding: 6 mg/day astaxanthin for 12 weeks lowered serum MDA and cytokines and increased oocytes, MII oocytes and high-quality embryos.

references.authors: Setchell KD, Brown NM, Lydeking-Olsen E
references.title: The clinical importance of the metabolite equol-a clue to the effectiveness of soy and its isoflavones.
references.finding: Equol is made only by gut bacteria from daidzein, and only some adults produce it; the producer/non-producer split may explain inconsistent soy trial results.

references.authors: Shafie A, Aleyasin A, Saffari M, et al.
references.title: Astaxanthin improves assisted reproductive technology outcomes in poor ovarian responders through alleviating oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis: a randomized clinical trial.
references.finding: 12 mg/day astaxanthin for 8 weeks increased oocytes retrieved, MII oocytes and high-quality embryos and lowered serum MDA and follicular-fluid IL-6.

references.authors: Vanegas JC, Afeiche MC, Gaskins AJ, et al.
references.title: Soy food intake and treatment outcomes of women undergoing assisted reproductive technology.
references.finding: Higher soy isoflavone intake was associated with higher live-birth rates in ART (OR ~1.8 for 2.6-28 mg/day vs none).

references.authors: Zhang Y, Bai J, Cui Z, et al.
references.title: Polyamine metabolite spermidine rejuvenates oocyte quality by enhancing mitophagy during female reproductive aging.
references.finding: Ovarian spermidine falls with age in mice; supplementation improved follicle development, oocyte maturation and fertility of aged mice by enhancing mitophagy.

references.authors: Arsenaki E, Stathi D, Triantafyllidis KK, et al.
references.title: The effects of ketogenic diet on polycystic ovary syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: In mostly overweight women with PCOS, ketogenic diets reduced weight (-10.8 kg), LH and insulin resistance and shortened cycle length pre-post, and beat other diets for weight and LH; androgen results were inconsistent and heterogeneity high.

references.authors: Cannarella R, Rubulotta M, Leonardi A, et al.
references.title: Effects of ketogenic diets on polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: High-fat ketogenic and very-low-energy ketogenic diets improved weight, glucose, HOMA, triglycerides and LH in PCOS; two RCTs found no weight advantage over low-calorie diets.

references.authors: Chavarro JE, Rich-Edwards JW, Rosner BA, et al.
references.title: A prospective study of dietary carbohydrate quantity and quality in relation to risk of ovulatory infertility.
references.finding: Highest vs lowest quintile of total carbohydrate (RR 1.91) and glycaemic load (RR 1.92) was associated with ovulatory infertility in the Nurses' Health Study II.

references.authors: de Amorim ALB, Rodrigues EF, Sussi EL, et al.
references.title: Carbohydrate restriction during lactation: A systematic review.
references.finding: Carbohydrate restriction during breastfeeding appears repeatedly in case reports of lactation ketoacidosis requiring hospital care.

references.authors: Desrosiers TA, Siega-Riz AM, Mosley BS, et al.
references.title: Low carbohydrate diets may increase risk of neural tube defects.
references.finding: Women with restricted periconceptional carbohydrate intake (<= 5th percentile) had half the dietary folic acid and 30% higher odds of a neural-tube-defect pregnancy (aOR 1.30, 1.02-1.67).

references.authors: Liu S, Yao Q, Li X, et al.
references.title: Effects of a ketogenic diet on reproductive and metabolic phenotypes in mice with polycystic ovary syndrome†.
references.finding: In DHEA-induced PCOS mice a 3-week ketogenic diet lowered weight and glucose, improved ovarian function in some mice and reduced ovarian inflammation and apoptosis, but impaired glucose tolerance.

references.authors: Mavropoulos JC, Yancy WS, Hepburn J, et al.
references.title: The effects of a low-carbohydrate, ketogenic diet on the polycystic ovary syndrome: a pilot study.
references.finding: A < 20 g/day carbohydrate diet for 24 weeks cut weight 12%, free testosterone 22%, LH/FSH 36% and fasting insulin 54% in PCOS; two women conceived.

references.authors: Shang Y, Zhou H, He R, et al.
references.title: Dietary Modification for Reproductive Health in Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: Dietary interventions in PCOS increased clinical pregnancy, ovulation and menstrual regularity and lowered miscarriage; low-carbohydrate diets were the best subgroup for reproductive outcomes.

references.authors: Sussman D, Ellegood J, Henkelman M
references.title: A gestational ketogenic diet alters maternal metabolic status as well as offspring physiological growth and brain structure in the neonatal mouse.
references.finding: Gestational ketogenic diet lowered fertility and litter size in mice, put dams at risk of fatal ketoacidosis in lactation, and slowed offspring growth with altered brain structure.

references.authors: van der Louw EJ, Williams TJ, Henry-Barron BJ, et al.
references.title: Ketogenic diet therapy for epilepsy during pregnancy: A case series.
references.finding: Two women with epilepsy stayed on ketogenic/modified Atkins therapy in pregnancy with fewer seizures; one infant had ear deformities of unknown significance; safety not established.

references.authors: Whatley EG, Truong TT, Wilhelm D, et al.
references.title: β-hydroxybutyrate reduces blastocyst viability via trophectoderm-mediated metabolic aberrations in mice.
references.finding: Culturing mouse embryos with BHB at ketogenic-diet levels (2 mmol/L) slowed development, disturbed glycolysis and reduced fetal viability after transfer in a sex-specific way.

references.authors: Whatley EG, Harvey AJ, Gardner DK
references.title: A maternal ketogenic diet alters oviduct fluid nutrients and embryo histone acetylation in mice.
references.finding: A maternal ketogenic diet for 24-27 days raised BHB in mouse blood and oviduct fluid, delayed blastocyst development and reduced trophectoderm histone acetylation.

references.authors: Zala SM, Santos R, Strasser E, et al.
references.title: Sex-dependent effects of a gestational ketogenic diet on offspring birth and lifespan.
references.finding: A ketogenic diet in the second half of mouse pregnancy reduced litter size and the proportion of female pups and shortened male offspring lifespan.

references.authors: Zhang X, Zheng Y, Guo Y, et al.
references.title: The Effect of Low Carbohydrate Diet on Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
references.finding: Low-carbohydrate diets (< 45% energy) lowered BMI, HOMA-IR and LDL in PCOS; those lasting > 4 weeks raised SHBG and FSH and lowered testosterone.

references.authors: Al-Taiar A, Rahman ME, Salama M, et al.
references.title: Impacts of Ramadan fasting during pregnancy on pregnancy and birth outcomes: An umbrella review.
references.finding: Umbrella review: insufficient evidence that Ramadan fasting in pregnancy shortens gestation or reduces birth weight, but evidence quality is low and no firm guidance is possible.

references.authors: Alvero R, Kimzey L, Sebring N, et al.
references.title: Effects of fasting on neuroendocrine function and follicle development in lean women.
references.finding: In lean women a 72-h follicular-phase fast cut LH pulses 19%; 2 of 7 fasted cycles were anovulatory and follicular phases lengthened.

references.authors: Cienfuegos S, Corapi S, Gabel K, et al.
references.title: Effect of Intermittent Fasting on Reproductive Hormone Levels in Females and Males: A Review of Human Trials.
references.finding: Review of human trials: IF lowers testosterone/free androgen index and raises SHBG in premenopausal women with obesity, does not change oestrogen or gonadotropins, and lowers testosterone in lean active young men.

references.authors: Glazier JD, Hayes DJL, Hussain S, et al.
references.title: The effect of Ramadan fasting during pregnancy on perinatal outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Ramadan fasting in pregnancy did not affect birth weight or preterm delivery; lower placental weight came mainly from one large study; no perinatal mortality data.

references.authors: Li C, Xing C, Zhang J, et al.
references.title: Eight-hour time-restricted feeding improves endocrine and metabolic profiles in women with anovulatory polycystic ovary syndrome.
references.finding: 5 weeks of 8-h TRE (single arm) lowered weight, testosterone, free androgen index, insulin and hsCRP, raised SHBG, and improved menstrual regularity in 11 of 15 women.

references.authors: Loucks AB, Thuma JR
references.title: Luteinizing hormone pulsatility is disrupted at a threshold of energy availability in regularly menstruating women.
references.finding: LH pulsatility was unaffected at an energy availability of 30 kcal/kg lean mass/day but disrupted below that threshold (10-20 kcal/kg).

references.authors: Metzger BE, Ravnikar V, Vileisis RA, et al.
references.title: "Accelerated starvation" and the skipped breakfast in late normal pregnancy.
references.finding: Extending the overnight fast from 12 to 18 h in late pregnancy ('skipped breakfast') caused falling glucose and rising fatty acids and beta-hydroxybutyrate ('accelerated starvation'); non-pregnant women barely changed.

references.authors: Mountjoy M, Ackerman KE, Bailey DM, et al.
references.title: 2023 International Olympic Committee's (IOC) consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs).
references.finding: IOC consensus on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport: low energy availability impairs reproductive, bone, metabolic and other systems in all sexes.

references.authors: Olson BR, Cartledge T, Sebring N, et al.
references.title: Short-term fasting affects luteinizing hormone secretory dynamics but not reproductive function in normal-weight sedentary women.
references.finding: A 3-day mid-follicular fast reduced LH pulses but did not alter follicle growth, ovulation or cycle length in normal-weight women.

references.authors: Ranneh Y, Hamsho M, Shkorfu W, et al.
references.title: Effect of Intermittent Fasting on Anthropometric Measurements, Metabolic Profile, and Hormones in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: In PCOS, IF reduced weight (-4.25 kg), insulin resistance, free androgen index and DHEA-S and raised SHBG; total testosterone and AMH did not change.

references.authors: Rizzo T, Metzger BE, Burns WJ, et al.
references.title: Correlations between antepartum maternal metabolism and intelligence of offspring.
references.finding: Higher third-trimester maternal beta-hydroxybutyrate correlated with lower offspring IQ scores at ages 2-5 (r about -0.2), observational.

references.authors: Talebi S, Shab-Bidar S, Moini A, et al.
references.title: The effects of time-restricted eating alone or in combination with probiotic supplementation in comparison with a calorie-restricted diet on endocrine and metabolic profiles in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: A randomized clinical trial.
references.finding: 8 weeks of 14:10 early TRE (with or without probiotics) gave no greater weight loss or menstrual, androgen or metabolic improvement than daily calorie restriction.

references.authors: Bach CC, Vested A, Jørgensen KT, et al.
references.title: Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances and measures of human fertility: a systematic review.
references.finding: Little consistent evidence that PFAS affect semen quality or hormones in men; associations with longer time to pregnancy appear in parous women and are most likely not causal.

references.authors: Björvang RD, Hassan J, Stefopoulou M, et al.
references.title: Persistent organic pollutants and the size of ovarian reserve in reproductive-aged women.
references.finding: PFAS were not associated with AMH or follicle density, whereas some organochlorines (HCB, PCBs) were linked to fewer non-growing follicles.

references.authors: Cohen NJ, Yao M, Midya V, et al.
references.title: Exposure to perfluoroalkyl substances and women's fertility outcomes in a Singaporean population-based preconception cohort.
references.finding: Each quartile increase in individual PFAS (PFDA, PFOS) was associated with 5-10% lower fecundability and lower odds of clinical pregnancy.

references.authors: Fei C, McLaughlin JK, Lipworth L, et al.
references.title: Maternal levels of perfluorinated chemicals and subfecundity.
references.finding: Higher plasma PFOS and PFOA were associated with longer time to pregnancy (fecundity odds ratios ~0.6-0.75 in upper quartiles).

references.authors: Fei C, Weinberg CR, Olsen J
references.title: Commentary: perfluorinated chemicals and time to pregnancy: a link based on reverse causation?
references.finding: Commentary by Fei, Weinberg and Olsen asking whether PFAS-time-to-pregnancy links reflect reverse causation (longer gaps since last pregnancy/breastfeeding let PFAS build up).

references.authors: Hong A, Zhuang L, Cui W, et al.
references.title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure in women seeking in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer treatment (IVF-ET) in China: Blood-follicular transfer and associations with IVF-ET outcomes.
references.finding: PFAS crossed readily from blood into follicular fluid (transfer 0.65-0.92) but showed no clear association with IVF outcomes.

references.authors: Wang W, Zhou W, Wu S, et al.
references.title: Perfluoroalkyl substances exposure and risk of polycystic ovarian syndrome related infertility in Chinese women.
references.finding: Most PFAS did not differ between PCOS-related infertility cases and controls; only PFDoA was associated with higher odds (OR 3.0 top vs bottom tertile).

references.authors: Whitworth KW, Haug LS, Baird DD, et al.
references.title: Perfluorinated compounds and subfecundity in pregnant women.
references.finding: Higher PFOS/PFOA was linked to subfecundity only in parous women (OR ~2.1), not in nulliparous women (OR 0.5-0.7), pointing to reverse causation.

references.authors: Xu J, Wang Q, Jiao X, et al.
references.title: Association between Perfluorooctanoic Acid-Related Poor Embryo Quality and Metabolite Alterations in Human Follicular Fluid during IVF: A Cohort Study.
references.finding: A follicular-fluid PFAS mixture, driven by PFOA, was associated with a lower high-quality embryo rate and lower clinical pregnancy.

references.authors: Zhan W, Qiu W, Ao Y, et al.
references.title: Environmental Exposure to Emerging Alternatives of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances and Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome in Women Diagnosed with Infertility: A Mixture Analysis.
references.finding: A PFAS mixture, led by emerging alternatives (6:2 Cl-PFESA, HFPO-DA), was associated with higher odds of PCOS (OR 1.20 per ln-unit).

references.authors: Anonymous
references.title: Treatment and Management of Mental Health Conditions During Pregnancy and Postpartum: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 5.
references.finding: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 5 on treating perinatal depression and anxiety, supporting SSRIs as first-line pharmacotherapy and individualized decisions rather than stopping effective treatment.

references.authors: Casilla-Lennon MM, Meltzer-Brody S, Steiner AZ
references.title: The effect of antidepressants on fertility.
references.finding: Cycle-specific antidepressant use was associated with lower fecundability (FR 0.75, CI crossing 1; 0.66 after adjusting for depression history), with confounding by depression unresolved.

references.authors: Cesta CE, Rotem R, Bateman BT, et al.
references.title: Safety of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Other Second-Line Antidiabetics in Early Pregnancy.
references.n: 51,826 infants of mothers with type 2 diabetes (Nordic, US, Israel)
references.finding: First-trimester GLP-1 agonist exposure was not associated with more major congenital malformations than insulin (adjusted RR 0.95, 0.72-1.26).

references.authors: Chen X, Yang Y, Chen L, et al.
references.title: Pregnancy outcomes and birth defects in offspring following Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs exposure during pregnancy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Early-pregnancy NSAID exposure was associated with more congenital anomalies (OR 1.28) and major birth defects (OR 1.19); miscarriage association was not significant (OR 1.20).

references.authors: Dilbaz B, Ateş Ç
references.title: The effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on fertility, contraception, and pregnancy: clinical perspectives.
references.journal: Eur J Contracept Reprod Health Care
references.finding: GLP-1 agonists help obesity-related infertility (notably PCOS); clinicians should counsel on contraceptive reliability, ensure washout before conception and note limited pregnancy-safety data.

references.authors: Drummond RF, Seif KE, Reece EA
references.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use in pregnancy: a review.
references.finding: AJOG review: malformation data lack glycemic-control information, so periconceptional safety cannot be concluded; recommends contraception for all patients on GLP-1 agonists.

references.authors: Evans-Hoeker EA, Eisenberg E, Diamond MP, et al.
references.title: Major depression, antidepressant use, and male and female fertility.
references.n: 1650 women and 1608 men in infertility trials
references.finding: Active major depression in the male partner lowered conception; maternal antidepressant use (n=90) was associated with first-trimester pregnancy loss.

references.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Novo Nordisk
references.title: WEGOVY (semaglutide) injection, prescribing information (revised 06/2021)
references.finding: Label section 8.3: discontinue semaglutide at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy because of its long half-life; discontinue when pregnancy is recognized.

references.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Eli Lilly
references.title: ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) injection, prescribing information (revised 11/2023)
references.finding: A single 5 mg tirzepatide dose cut ethinyl estradiol Cmax 59% and AUC 20%; users of oral contraceptives should switch to a non-oral method or add a barrier method for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose escalation.

references.authors: Forslund M, Wändell P, Forsberg L, et al.
references.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment in women with polycystic ovary syndrome-a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Meta-analysis informing the PCOS guideline: GLP-1 agonists as add-on lowered BMI by 1.38 kg/m2 (low certainty); evidence on reproductive, metabolic and psychological outcomes remains insufficient.

references.authors: Girum T, Wasie A
references.title: Return of fertility after discontinuation of contraception: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: 83.1% of women conceived within 12 months of stopping contraception, with no difference between hormonal methods and IUDs or by duration of pill use.

references.authors: Hall SD, Wang Z, Huang SM, et al.
references.title: The interaction between St John's wort and an oral contraceptive.
references.finding: St John's wort increased norethindrone clearance and halved ethinyl estradiol half-life; breakthrough bleeding rose from 2 to 7 of 12 women.

references.authors: Han Y, Li Y, He B
references.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists versus metformin in PCOS: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Versus metformin, GLP-1 agonists improved insulin sensitivity and lowered BMI and waist more in PCOS, with more nausea; evidence moderate to low.

references.authors: Hviid KVR, Banasik K, Mortensen LH, et al.
references.title: Periconceptional GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure and obstetric outcomes: a Danish nationwide cohort study.
references.finding: Periconceptional liraglutide or semaglutide was linked to preterm birth only in women with diabetes (aOR ~1.7-1.8), not in those using them for weight management, pointing to the underlying diabetes.

references.authors: Li DK, Ferber JR, Odouli R, et al.
references.title: Use of nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs during pregnancy and the risk of miscarriage.
references.finding: NSAID use around conception was associated with more miscarriage (aHR 1.89), stronger for early loss and longer use; acetaminophen users were used as an indication control.

references.authors: Micu MC, Micu R, Ostensen M
references.title: Luteinized unruptured follicle syndrome increased by inactive disease and selective cyclooxygenase 2 inhibitors in women with inflammatory arthropathies.
references.n: 59 monitored cycles with NSAIDs vs untreated cycles in women with inflammatory arthritis
references.finding: Continuous periovulatory NSAIDs caused luteinized unruptured follicle in 35.6% of cycles vs 3.4% untreated; etoricoxib was the main culprit and ibuprofen 1600 mg/day caused none.

references.authors: Nillni YI, Wesselink AK, Gradus JL, et al.
references.title: Depression, anxiety, and psychotropic medication use and fecundability.
references.finding: Severe depressive symptoms lowered fecundability (FR 0.62) regardless of treatment; psychotropic medication use itself did not appear to harm fecundability.

references.authors: Ozbek L, Shah E, Al-Shiab R, et al.
references.title: Safety of GLP-1 and Dual GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonists in Preconception, Pregnancy, and Lactation: A Systematic Review of Maternal, Fetal, and Neonatal Outcomes.
references.finding: Periconceptional or early-pregnancy GLP-1-based therapy was not consistently linked to malformations, growth restriction, stillbirth or neonatal death; data on continued use through pregnancy are limited.

references.authors: Salamun V, Jensterle M, Janez A, et al.
references.title: Liraglutide increases IVF pregnancy rates in obese PCOS women with poor response to first-line reproductive treatments: a pilot randomized study.
references.finding: Pilot open-label trial: 12 weeks of liraglutide 1.2 mg plus metformin before IVF (with a 4-week washout) gave higher pregnancy rate per transfer (85.7% vs 28.6%) than metformin alone despite similar weight loss.

references.authors: Skelley JW, Swearengin K, York AL, et al.
references.title: The impact of tirzepatide and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists on oral hormonal contraception.
references.finding: Tirzepatide significantly reduced oral-contraceptive exposure (AUC, Cmax) via delayed gastric emptying, whereas studies of other GLP-1 agonists showed no clinically significant effect.

references.authors: Smith G, Roberts R, Hall C, et al.
references.title: Reversible ovulatory failure associated with the development of luteinized unruptured follicles in women with inflammatory arthritis taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.
references.finding: Three women with inflammatory arthritis had recurrent luteinized unruptured follicles on NSAIDs, with normal ovulation after stopping.

references.authors: Stone S, Khamashta MA, Nelson-Piercy C
references.title: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and reversible female infertility: is there a link?
references.finding: COX-2 inhibition blocks follicle rupture; animal data and three small clinical studies link regular NSAIDs to reversible anovulation, so withdrawal should be considered during fertility work-up.

references.authors: Sylvester C, Menke M, Gopalan P
references.title: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors and Fertility: Considerations for Couples Trying to Conceive.
references.finding: Insufficient evidence that SSRIs reduce female fertility or IVF outcomes; six of seven mostly poor-quality male studies found adverse effects on semen.

references.authors: Teede HJ, Tay CT, Laven JJE, et al.
references.title: Recommendations From the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
references.finding: 2023 International Evidence-based PCOS Guideline (endorsed by ASRM, ESHRE, Endocrine Society, ESE): 254 recommendations including letrozole as first-line ovulation induction, metformin for metabolic features, and anti-obesity medicines alongside lifestyle.

references.authors: Yland JJ, Bresnick KA, Hatch EE, et al.
references.title: Pregravid contraceptive use and fecundability: prospective cohort study.
references.finding: Return to normal fertility took about 5-8 cycles after injectables (FR 0.65), 4 after the patch, 3 after pill or ring and 2 after IUDs or implants; total years of hormonal use did not matter.

references.authors: Aktoz F
references.title: The role of endometrial scratching in IVF/ICSI: a critical appraisal of individual participant data meta-analysis
references.finding: Critical letter questioning the methods and conclusions of the endometrial scratching IPD meta-analysis (with author reply).

references.authors: Armstrong S, Bhide P, Jordan V, et al.
references.title: Time-lapse systems for embryo incubation and assessment in assisted reproduction
references.finding: Cochrane: low to very low quality evidence; no clear difference in live birth/ongoing pregnancy with time-lapse systems (OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.67-1.23).

references.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
references.title: Testing and interpreting measures of ovarian reserve: a committee opinion
references.finding: ASRM: ovarian reserve markers (AMH, AFC, FSH) predict egg yield after stimulation but are poor predictors of reproductive potential independent of age.

references.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
references.title: Evidence-based outcomes after oocyte cryopreservation for donor oocyte in vitro fertilization and planned oocyte cryopreservation: a guideline
references.finding: ASRM guideline: insufficient evidence to predict live birth after planned egg freezing; outcomes appear better when frozen younger; neonatal outcomes similar to fresh eggs.

references.authors: Ethics Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
references.title: Planned oocyte cryopreservation to preserve future reproductive potential: an Ethics Committee opinion
references.finding: ASRM Ethics Committee: planned egg freezing is ethically permissible; people must be told about uncertain efficacy and long-term effects.

references.authors: Barrenetxea G, Celis R, Barrenetxea J, et al.
references.title: Intraovarian platelet-rich plasma injection and IVF outcomes in patients with poor ovarian response: a double-blind randomized controlled trial
references.finding: Double-blind RCT: intraovarian PRP slightly raised cumulative mature eggs (10.45 vs 8.91) over three retrievals but not euploid blastocysts (0.81 vs 0.81).

references.authors: Bhide P, Chan DYL, Lanz D, et al.
references.title: Clinical effectiveness and safety of time-lapse imaging systems for embryo incubation and selection in in-vitro fertilisation treatment (TILT): a multicentre, three-parallel-group, double-blind, randomised controlled trial
references.finding: TILT trial: live birth 33.7% with time-lapse imaging, 36.6% with undisturbed culture and 33.0% with standard care (aOR 1.04 and 1.20, both non-significant).

references.authors: Blakemore JK, Grifo JA, DeVore SM, et al.
references.title: Planned oocyte cryopreservation-10-15-year follow-up: return rates and cycle outcomes
references.finding: 10-15-year follow-up of planned egg freezing (mean age 38.2): 38.1% returned; live birth 33.8% among those with outcomes; 58.9% non-use.

references.authors: Boomsma CM, Kamath MS, Keay SD, et al.
references.title: Peri-implantation glucocorticoid administration for assisted reproductive technology cycles
references.finding: Cochrane: uncertain whether peri-implantation glucocorticoids improve live birth (OR 1.37, 95% CI 0.69-2.71; very low certainty).

references.authors: Broer SL, Dólleman M, Opmeer BC, et al.
references.title: AMH and AFC as predictors of excessive response in controlled ovarian hyperstimulation: a meta-analysis
references.finding: AMH and AFC both predict excessive ovarian response (sensitivity ~82%, specificity 76-80%).

references.authors: Broer SL, van Disseldorp J, Broeze KA, et al.
references.title: Added value of ovarian reserve testing on patient characteristics in the prediction of ovarian response and ongoing pregnancy: an individual patient data approach
references.finding: AMH and AFC predict poor ovarian response well (AUC 0.78 and 0.76) but add nothing to age for predicting ongoing pregnancy after IVF.

references.authors: Burton GJ, Jauniaux E
references.title: Oxidative stress
references.journal: Best Pract Res Clin Obstet Gynaecol
references.finding: Review of reactive oxygen species in the placenta: physiological signalling at low levels, and involvement in miscarriage, pre-eclampsia and membrane rupture at high levels.

references.authors: Burton GJ, Redman CW, Roberts JM, et al.
references.title: Pre-eclampsia: pathophysiology and clinical implications
references.finding: BMJ review: pre-eclampsia arises from syncytiotrophoblast stress; early-onset from defective placentation, late-onset from placental senescence plus maternal cardiometabolic predisposition.

references.authors: Capalbo A, Poli M, Rienzi L, et al.
references.title: Mosaic human preimplantation embryos and their developmental potential in a prospective, non-selection clinical trial
references.finding: Non-selection trial (Igenomix authors): low- and medium-grade mosaic embryos had live birth and miscarriage rates equivalent to euploid embryos, implying PGT-A labels can discard viable embryos.

references.authors: Cobo A, García-Velasco JA, Coello A, et al.
references.title: Oocyte vitrification as an efficient option for elective fertility preservation
references.finding: Elective egg freezing: cumulative live birth with 10-15 vitrified eggs reached ~85% at <=35 years vs ~36% plateau at >=36; 8-10 mature eggs needed for reasonable success; 9.3% had returned.

references.authors: Cobo A, García-Velasco JA
references.title: Why all women should freeze their eggs
references.finding: IVI review arguing for elective egg freezing: success is best when frozen before 35, but studies show freezing is most cost-effective at 37-38.

references.authors: Conde-Agudelo A, Romero R, Kusanovic JP, et al.
references.title: Supplementation with vitamins C and E during pregnancy for the prevention of preeclampsia and other adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes: a systematic review and metaanalysis
references.finding: Vitamins C and E did not prevent pre-eclampsia (9.6% vs 9.6%) and increased gestational hypertension and premature rupture of membranes.

references.authors: Cornelisse S, Zagers M, Kostova E, et al.
references.title: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidies (abnormal number of chromosomes) in in vitro fertilisation
references.finding: Cochrane: uncertain whether PGT-A increases cumulative live birth; low to moderate quality evidence; possible reduction in miscarriage.

references.authors: Craciunas L, Tsampras N, Raine-Fenning N, et al.
references.title: Intrauterine administration of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) for subfertile women undergoing assisted reproduction
references.finding: Cochrane: intrauterine hCG >=500 IU improved live birth only with cleavage-stage transfer (moderate quality); insufficient evidence for blastocyst transfer; no reduction in miscarriage.

references.authors: Depmann M, Broer SL, van der Schouw YT, et al.
references.title: Can we predict age at natural menopause using ovarian reserve tests or mother's age at menopause? A systematic literature review
references.finding: AMH is the most promising predictor of age at natural menopause but prediction intervals are too wide for individual use.

references.authors: Doyle JO, Richter KS, Lim J, et al.
references.title: Successful elective and medically indicated oocyte vitrification and warming for autologous in vitro fertilization, with predicted birth probabilities for fertility preservation according to number of cryopreserved oocytes and age at retrieval
references.finding: Vitrified eggs performed as well as fresh; overall vitrified egg-to-baby efficiency was 6.4% per egg, falling with age at retrieval.

references.authors: Doyle N, Jahandideh S, Hill MJ, et al.
references.title: Effect of Timing by Endometrial Receptivity Testing vs Standard Timing of Frozen Embryo Transfer on Live Birth in Patients Undergoing In Vitro Fertilization: A Randomized Clinical Trial
references.finding: Euploid frozen transfers timed by endometrial receptivity testing did not improve live birth (58.5% vs 61.9%; RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.79-1.13).

references.authors: Duley L, Meher S, Hunter KE, et al.
references.title: Antiplatelet agents for preventing pre-eclampsia and its complications
references.finding: Cochrane: antiplatelet agents cut proteinuric pre-eclampsia by 18% (RR 0.82; NNT 61), preterm birth by 9% and fetal/neonatal death by 14%; may slightly increase postpartum haemorrhage.

references.authors: ESHRE Guideline Group on Female Fertility Preservation
references.title: ESHRE guideline: female fertility preservation
references.finding: ESHRE female fertility preservation guideline covering medical and age-related egg freezing; 78 recommendations, mostly low or very low quality evidence.

references.authors: ESHRE Add-ons working group; Lundin K, Bentzen JG, Bozdag G, et al.
references.title: Good practice recommendations on add-ons in reproductive medicine
references.finding: ESHRE good practice recommendations on 42 add-ons: none based on high-quality evidence; not recommended include endometrial receptivity tests, immune testing and immunomodulators (Intralipid, IVIG), glucocorticoids, assisted hatching, time-lapse imaging (to improve live birth), intrauterine hCG, intrauterine and intraovarian PRP, mitochondrial replacement, adjuncts during stimulation (growth hormone, DHEA, testosterone), oral antioxidants and ICSI for non-male factor; PGT-A, endometrial scratching, MACS, PICSI and IMSI 'not recommended for routine clinical use'; microfluidics 'can be considered'; hyaluronan in transfer medium 'recommended' (with single embryo transfer).

references.authors: ESHRE Working Group on Recurrent Implantation Failure; Cimadomo D, de Los Santos MJ, Griesinger G, et al.
references.title: ESHRE good practice recommendations on recurrent implantation failure
references.finding: ESHRE recurrent implantation failure recommendations: RIF defined by a >60% predicted cumulative implantation chance; investigations and interventions graded recommended, to consider, or not recommended.

references.authors: Finkelstein JS, Lee H, Karlamangla A, et al.
references.title: Antimullerian Hormone and Impending Menopause in Late Reproductive Age: The Study of Women's Health Across the Nation
references.n: SWAN women in late reproductive age
references.finding: In women in their late 40s, very low AMH (<10 pg/mL) predicted the final period within 12 months (51-79% by age); AMH outperformed FSH.

references.authors: Franasiak JM, Forman EJ, Hong KH, et al.
references.title: The nature of aneuploidy with increasing age of the female partner: a review of 15,169 consecutive trophectoderm biopsies evaluated with comprehensive chromosomal screening
references.finding: Embryo aneuploidy rose predictably after 26; chance of no euploid embryo 2-6% at 26-37, 33% at 42, 53% at 44.

references.authors: Gardner DK, Kuramoto T, Tanaka M, et al.
references.title: Prospective randomized multicentre comparison on sibling oocytes comparing G-Series media system with antioxidants versus standard G-Series media system
references.finding: Antioxidants (acetyl-L-carnitine, NAC, alpha-lipoic acid) in culture media raised good day-3 embryos (50.2% vs 40.7%) and, in women 35-40, ongoing pregnancy (50% vs 25.8%); no live-birth primary outcome.

references.authors: Goldman RH, Racowsky C, Farland LV, et al.
references.title: Predicting the likelihood of live birth for elective oocyte cryopreservation: a counseling tool for physicians and patients
references.finding: Counselling model predicting chance of 1-3 live births from age at retrieval and number of mature eggs frozen; derived from fresh ICSI data, not returning egg-freezers.

references.authors: Goold I, Savulescu J
references.title: In favour of freezing eggs for non-medical reasons
references.finding: Bioethics argument in favour of egg freezing for non-medical reasons (autonomy, equality in work, time to find a partner).

references.authors: Heneghan C, Spencer EA, Bobrovitz N, et al.
references.title: Lack of evidence for interventions offered in UK fertility centres
references.finding: Oxford CEBM analysis: most interventions offered on UK fertility centre websites lacked supporting high-quality evidence.

references.authors: Herlihy NS, Cakiroglu Y, Whitehead C, et al.
references.title: Effect of intraovarian platelet-rich plasma injection on IVF outcomes in women with poor ovarian response: the PROVA randomized controlled trial
references.finding: PROVA trial: intraovarian PRP did not change mature eggs (2.8 vs 3.1), euploid blastocysts, AMH, AFC or sustained implantation.

references.authors: Heymann D, Vidal L, Or Y, et al.
references.title: Hyaluronic acid in embryo transfer media for assisted reproductive technologies
references.finding: Cochrane: functional hyaluronan (0.5 mg/mL) in transfer medium probably raises live birth (RR 1.21, 95% CI 1.10-1.31; moderate certainty; ~33% -> 37-44%) but also raises multiple pregnancy (RR 1.45).

references.authors: Heymann D, Vidal L, Shoham Z, et al.
references.title: The effect of hyaluronic acid in embryo transfer media in donor oocyte cycles and autologous oocyte cycles: a systematic review and meta-analysis
references.finding: Hyaluronan transfer medium raised live birth from 32% to 39% with women's own eggs (RR 1.22; NNT 14), with more multiple pregnancies (NNH 13); little effect in donor-egg cycles.

references.authors: Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority (HFEA)
references.title: Treatment add-ons with limited evidence (HFEA add-ons rating list)
references.finding: HFEA traffic-light ratings for 'chances of having a baby' (page reviewed 28 Sep 2026; ratings set by SCAAC): yellow/amber (unclear) for endometrial scratching, hyaluronate-enriched transfer medium and elective freeze-all; grey (insufficient evidence) for assisted hatching, androgens, intralipids, IMSI, intrauterine culture, microbiome testing and SDF-guided treatments; black (no effect) for time-lapse imaging and PICSI; red (no benefit and/or safety concerns) for endometrial receptivity testing, IVIG, steroids, PRP and PGT-A (PGT-A rated green for reducing miscarriage). No green rating for live birth.

references.authors: Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority (HFEA)
references.title: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP): treatment add-on rating
references.finding: Intraovarian PRP for poor/diminished ovarian reserve and intrauterine PRP for thin endometrium, recurrent implantation failure, Asherman's syndrome and recurrent pregnancy loss all rated red (safety concerns, no moderate/high-quality evidence); not rated for most patients because there is no medical reason to offer it. Reviewed 27 Feb 2026.

references.authors: Iwarsson E, Bergh C, Lundin K, et al.
references.title: PGT-A, the theory versus the evidence: a systematic review on efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness
references.finding: Systematic review (Swedish HTA-style): live birth per randomised woman was similar with and without PGT-A, both first transfer (OR 1.16, 0.94-1.45) and cumulative (OR 0.87, 0.64-1.19), including over 35; no shorter time to live birth; PGT-A nearly doubles IVF cost.

references.authors: Kieslinger DC, Vergouw CG, Ramos L, et al.
references.title: Clinical outcomes of uninterrupted embryo culture with or without time-lapse-based embryo selection versus interrupted standard culture (SelecTIMO): a three-armed, multicentre, double-blind, randomised controlled trial
references.finding: SelecTIMO: 12-month cumulative ongoing pregnancy 50.8% (time-lapse selection), 50.9% (time-lapse culture) and 49.4% (standard), p=0.85.

references.authors: Labarta E, de Los Santos MJ, Herraiz S, et al.
references.title: Autologous mitochondrial transfer as a complementary technique to intracytoplasmic sperm injection to improve embryo quality in patients undergoing in vitro fertilization-a randomized pilot study
references.finding: AUGMENT pilot RCT (stopped): autologous mitochondrial transfer gave fewer blastocysts (23.3% vs 41.1%) and equal live birth per transferred embryo (41.6% vs 41.2%).

references.authors: Lacey L, Hassan S, Franik S, et al.
references.title: Assisted hatching on assisted conception (in vitro fertilisation (IVF) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI))
references.finding: Cochrane: uncertain whether assisted hatching improves live birth (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.92-1.29; low quality); may slightly increase multiple pregnancy (OR 1.38).

references.authors: Lensen S, Osavlyuk D, Armstrong S, et al.
references.title: A Randomized Trial of Endometrial Scratching before In Vitro Fertilization
references.finding: PIP trial: endometrial scratching before IVF gave identical live birth to no intervention (26.1% vs 26.1%; aOR 1.00, 95% CI 0.78-1.27), with median pain 3.5/10.

references.authors: Lensen S, Hammarberg K, Polyakov A, et al.
references.title: How common is add-on use and how do patients decide whether to use them? A national survey of IVF patients
references.finding: In an Australian national survey, 82% of IVF patients had used at least one add-on, usually at extra cost; half assumed add-ons were known to be safe and 66% reported some regret.

references.authors: Li J, Chen Y, Liu C, et al.
references.title: Intravenous immunoglobulin treatment for repeated IVF/ICSI failure and unexplained infertility: a systematic review and a meta-analysis
references.finding: Meta-analysis mixing randomised and case-control studies reported higher live birth with IVIG after repeated IVF failure (RR 1.62); low-quality evidence.

references.authors: McCance DR, Holmes VA, Maresh MJ, et al.
references.title: Vitamins C and E for prevention of pre-eclampsia in women with type 1 diabetes (DAPIT): a randomised placebo-controlled trial
references.finding: DAPIT: vitamins C and E did not significantly reduce pre-eclampsia (15% vs 19%; RR 0.81, 0.59-1.12); authors suggested testing women with low antioxidant status.

references.authors: Mendoza M, Bonacina E, Garcia-Manau P, et al.
references.title: Aspirin Discontinuation at 24 to 28 Weeks' Gestation in Pregnancies at High Risk of Preterm Preeclampsia: A Randomized Clinical Trial
references.finding: StopPRE: stopping aspirin at 24-28 weeks in high-risk women with a normal sFlt-1:PlGF ratio was non-inferior to continuing (preterm pre-eclampsia 1.48% vs 1.73%).

references.authors: Mertes H
references.title: Does company-sponsored egg freezing promote or confine women's reproductive autonomy?
references.finding: Ethical analysis: employer-paid egg freezing is only liberating if women understand limits, feel no pressure and other family-friendly policies are kept; these conditions may be impossible to meet.

references.authors: Munné S, Kaplan B, Frattarelli JL, et al.
references.title: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy versus morphology as selection criteria for single frozen-thawed embryo transfer in good-prognosis patients: a multicenter randomized clinical trial
references.finding: STAR trial: PGT-A did not improve ongoing pregnancy per intention to treat (41.8% vs 43.5%); a post hoc gain per transfer in women 35-40 was not significant per intention to treat.

references.authors: Norman RJ, Alvino H, Hull LM, et al.
references.title: Human growth hormone for poor responders: a randomized placebo-controlled trial provides no evidence for improved live birth rate
references.finding: LIGHT trial (stopped early): growth hormone in previous poor responders gave 14.5% vs 13.7% live birth (OR 1.07, 0.37-3.10).

references.authors: Paulson RJ
references.title: Outcome of in vitro fertilization cycles with preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidies: let's be honest with one another
references.finding: Editorial arguing that PGT-A results should be reported per started cycle, because per-transfer success rates hide embryos lost to testing.

references.authors: Perera AK, Gan J, Afroz A, et al.
references.title: Endometrial injury in women undergoing in vitro fertilisation (IVF)
references.finding: Cochrane 2026: in low-risk-of-bias trials, the effect of endometrial injury on live birth is unclear (OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.98-1.28; moderate certainty), roughly 27% -> 27-32%; causes mild to moderate pain; conclusion unchanged from 2021.

references.authors: Poston L, Briley AL, Seed PT, et al.
references.title: Vitamin C and vitamin E in pregnant women at risk for pre-eclampsia (VIP trial): randomised placebo-controlled trial
references.finding: VIP trial: vitamin C 1000 mg + vitamin E 400 IU daily did not prevent pre-eclampsia (15% vs 16%) and increased low birthweight (28% vs 24%; RR 1.15).

references.authors: Roberts JM, Myatt L, Spong CY, et al.
references.title: Vitamins C and E to prevent complications of pregnancy-associated hypertension
references.finding: NICHD MFMU trial: vitamins C and E from 9-16 weeks did not reduce pregnancy-associated hypertension complications (6.1% vs 5.7%) or pre-eclampsia (7.2% vs 6.7%).

references.authors: Rolnik DL, Wright D, Poon LC, et al.
references.title: Aspirin versus Placebo in Pregnancies at High Risk for Preterm Preeclampsia
references.finding: ASPRE: aspirin 150 mg nightly from 11-14 to 36 weeks cut preterm pre-eclampsia from 4.3% to 1.6% (OR 0.38) in screen-positive women.

references.authors: Rubio C, Bellver J, Rodrigo L, et al.
references.title: In vitro fertilization with preimplantation genetic diagnosis for aneuploidies in advanced maternal age: a randomized, controlled study
references.n: 205 women of advanced maternal age (326 recruited)
references.finding: In women of advanced maternal age, PGT-A raised delivery per first transfer (52.9% vs 24.2%) and cut miscarriage (2.7% vs 39.0%) and time to pregnancy, but cumulative delivery per patient did not differ.

references.authors: Rumbold A, Ota E, Hori H, et al.
references.title: Vitamin E supplementation in pregnancy
references.finding: Cochrane: vitamin E (with C) did not reduce pre-eclampsia (RR 0.91) or stillbirth, lowered abruption (RR 0.64) but raised term prelabour rupture of membranes (RR 1.77).

references.authors: Simón C, Gómez C, Cabanillas S, et al.
references.title: A 5-year multicentre randomized controlled trial comparing personalized, frozen and fresh blastocyst transfer in IVF
references.finding: Igenomix-led trial of ERA-guided personalised transfer: intention-to-treat outcomes were comparable; per-protocol cumulative live birth was higher (71.2% vs 55.4%), but about 50% of patients dropped out.

references.authors: Singh N, Davis AA, Kumar S, et al.
references.title: The effect of administration of intravenous intralipid on pregnancy outcomes in women with implantation failure after IVF/ICSI with non-donor oocytes: A randomised controlled trial
references.journal: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
references.finding: Small RCT: intravenous intralipid after implantation failure raised live birth (28.8% vs 10%).

references.authors: Sood A, Mohiyiddeen G, Ahmad G, et al.
references.title: Growth hormone for in vitro fertilisation (IVF)
references.finding: Cochrane: in poor responders, growth hormone may raise live birth (OR 1.77, 95% CI 1.17-2.70) but the evidence is very low certainty; about 1.4 more eggs retrieved.

references.authors: Steiner AZ, Herring AH, Kesner JS, et al.
references.title: Antimüllerian hormone as a predictor of natural fecundability in women aged 30-42 years
references.finding: Pilot cohort: AMH <=0.7 ng/mL was associated with lower day-specific natural fecundability (FR 0.38, 95% CI 0.08-0.91).

references.authors: Steiner AZ, Pritchard D, Stanczyk FZ, et al.
references.title: Association Between Biomarkers of Ovarian Reserve and Infertility Among Older Women of Reproductive Age
references.finding: Time to Conceive cohort: low AMH (<0.7 ng/mL) or high FSH did not reduce the chance of natural conception (by 12 cycles, 84% vs 75% with normal AMH).

references.authors: Tiegs AW, Tao X, Zhan Y, et al.
references.title: A multicenter, prospective, blinded, nonselection study evaluating the predictive value of an aneuploid diagnosis using a targeted next-generation sequencing-based preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy assay and impact of biopsy
references.finding: Blinded non-selection study: embryos called aneuploid by NGS PGT-A essentially never led to delivery (0% clinical error), and biopsy did not reduce sustained implantation.

references.authors: Tilly JL, Woods DC
references.title: The obligate need for accuracy in reporting preclinical studies relevant to clinical trials: autologous germline mitochondrial supplementation for assisted human reproduction as a case study
references.finding: Review by the laboratory behind AUGMENT: three early uncontrolled studies (104 patients) suggested benefit, a fourth (57 patients) did not; argues safety concerns from a mouse study were misplaced.

references.authors: Davidson KW, Barry MJ, Mangione CM, et al.
references.title: Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement
references.finding: USPSTF (B): low-dose aspirin 81 mg/day after 12 weeks for people at high risk of pre-eclampsia.

references.authors: Vaidakis D, Papapanou M, Siristatidis CS
references.title: Autologous platelet-rich plasma for assisted reproduction
references.finding: Cochrane: very low-certainty evidence for intrauterine and intraovarian PRP; the only low-risk-of-bias intrauterine trial showed no clear effect on live birth (OR 1.10, 0.38-3.14).

references.authors: van Hoogenhuijze NE, Lahoz Casarramona G, Lensen S, et al.
references.title: Endometrial scratching in women undergoing IVF/ICSI: an individual participant data meta-analysis
references.finding: Individual-participant-data meta-analysis after integrity checks: scratching was associated with higher live birth (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.02-1.64), but sensitivity analyses were borderline (e.g. OR 1.22, 0.96-1.54) and no subgroup benefited more.

references.authors: Villar J, Purwar M, Merialdi M, et al.
references.title: World Health Organisation multicentre randomised trial of supplementation with vitamins C and E among pregnant women at high risk for pre-eclampsia in populations of low nutritional status from developing countries
references.finding: WHO trial in low-nutrition populations: vitamins C and E did not reduce pre-eclampsia (RR 1.0) or any maternal or perinatal outcome.

references.authors: Wennberg AL, Schildauer K, Brännström M
references.title: Elective oocyte freezing for nonmedical reasons: a 6-year report on utilization and in vitro fertilization results from a Swedish center
references.finding: Swedish elective egg freezing: 15% returned; cumulative live birth/ongoing pregnancy 63% if frozen at 36-37, 26% at 38-39, 0% at 40+.

references.authors: Yan J, Qin Y, Zhao H, et al.
references.title: Live Birth with or without Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Aneuploidy
references.finding: In women with 3+ good blastocysts, cumulative live birth was 77.2% with PGT-A vs 81.8% without (difference -4.6 points); pregnancy loss was 8.7% vs 12.6%.

references.authors: Zarek SM, Mitchell EM, Sjaarda LA, et al.
references.title: Is Anti-Müllerian Hormone Associated With Fecundability? Findings From the EAGeR Trial
references.finding: EAGeR trial cohort: low or high AMH was not associated with fecundability in women with prior losses (FOR 1.13 for low AMH).

references.authors: Carlomagno F, Tenuta M, Sansone A, et al.
references.title: Iron overload disorders in adults: a comprehensive review of gonadal function, reproductive, and sexual health
references.n: Systematic review: 1201 men, 2134 women with iron overload
references.finding: In iron overload disorders, 47% of men had hypogonadism and over half of those assessed had azoospermia or other sperm abnormalities; early chelation helps prevent but rarely reverses damage.

references.authors: Chavarro JE, Rich-Edwards JW, Rosner BA, et al.
references.title: Iron intake and risk of ovulatory infertility
references.finding: Women using iron supplements had 40% lower risk of ovulatory infertility (RR 0.60); heme iron was unrelated.

references.authors: Hahn KA, Wesselink AK, Wise LA, et al.
references.title: Iron Consumption Is Not Consistently Associated with Fecundability among North American and Danish Pregnancy Planners
references.n: 4662 pregnancy planners (Denmark n=1693, North America n=2969)
references.finding: Iron intake was not consistently associated with fecundability; supplements helped modestly in North America (FR 1.19) and in women with heavy menses.

references.authors: Institute of Medicine (US) Panel on Micronutrients
references.title: Dietary Reference Intakes for Vitamin A, Vitamin K, Arsenic, Boron, Chromium, Copper, Iodine, Iron, Manganese, Molybdenum, Nickel, Silicon, Vanadium, and Zinc
references.finding: IOM DRI report for vitamin A, copper, iodine, iron, manganese, zinc and others (ULs: zinc 40 mg, copper 10 mg, iron 45 mg, iodine 1100 ug, manganese 11 mg, preformed vitamin A 3000 ug).

references.authors: Khambalia AZ, Aimone A, Nagubandi P, et al.
references.title: High maternal iron status, dietary iron intake and iron supplement use in pregnancy and risk of gestational diabetes mellitus: a prospective study and systematic review
references.finding: Higher ferritin (OR 1.41 per unit), serum iron and heme iron intake were associated with gestational diabetes; two supplement trials showed no association.

references.authors: Ni Z, Li Y, Song D, et al.
references.title: Iron-overloaded follicular fluid increases the risk of endometriosis-related infertility by triggering granulosa cell ferroptosis and oocyte dysmaturity
references.finding: Iron-overloaded follicular fluid from women with endometriosis triggered granulosa-cell ferroptosis and impaired oocyte maturation in mouse models; vitamin E and deferoxamine helped.
